defect.summary: The H2C runner was derived from the H2A/Phase-13 lineage and inherited its start/completion AUDIT PAYLOAD identity strings. The completed run's audit payloads therefore mislabel the run as a Phase-13 clean-v3 run with protocol_identity 'R2 + R2A_LOSS_BINDING' and scientific_changes = 0, whereas H2C is a head-redesign run with exactly 1 scientific change.
defect.severity_scope: CONFINED TO RUNNER-GENERATED REPORTING PAYLOADS. The scientific state is CORRECT: the checkpoint's configuration.architecture.h2c_head records the frozen H2C head identity AND the frozen H2C protocol SHA, the state_dict carries the H2C head tensors (conv3x3 16x16x3x3, conv1x1 1x16x1x1), and the recorded loss is the correct retained H2A focal objective (CenterNetFocalLoss alpha=2.0 beta=4.0).
defect.distinct_from_h2b_precedent: The H2B defect was in the CHECKPOINT/RESUME CONTRACT (active objective identity) and required invalidating the attempt. Here the checkpoint is correct; only the reporting payload labels are wrong, so NO training restart is warranted.

repair_applied.runner_diff_confined_to_audit_identity_s: YES (all 22 machinery probes unchanged; implementation diff re-run: all_probes_unchanged = True, no non-UNCHANGED machinery item)
repair_applied.training_restarted: NO (not warranted - the checkpoint is correct)
repair_applied.consequence_for_future_resume: A resume of this completed run would now trip the runner_sha gate, because the checkpoint records the pre-fix runner SHA. Training is COMPLETE (72 epochs, early-stopped), so no resume is required. Flagged for supervisor awareness.
